rationale: Both races are close. Talarico leads Paxton by about 2-4 points in Texas polls, and El-Sayed leads Rogers by about 2-4 in Michigan, so each is roughly 50% and 65% on its own. The two outcomes are positively correlated, which puts the joint chance near 0.37. What would make this wrong: Texas polls have historically overstated Democrats (likely, about 50%), so I trimmed to 0.35. Web search budget ran out before a final check.

Base rate: Minnesota has not elected a Republican senator since 2002. Flanagan leads Tafoya by about 3-5 points across averages (RCP +3.4, Pollsmax +4.6). Cook moved the race to Lean D because of the fraud scandal. What would make this wrong: a polling miss toward the Republican tied to the scandal and undecided voters (about 15-20%), which this number already allows for.

The deposit rate is 2.50%. Analysts such as LBBW expect the next hike in December, when new projections come out, not on October 29. One result quoted an OIS-implied hike probability; I discarded it and flagged it here. What would make this wrong: an energy-driven inflation surprise prompts an early hike. That is unlikely given the ECB's preference for acting at projection meetings.

There has been no direct Israel-Iran fire since June, and Trump has pledged no strikes before the November 3 midterms. However, the NYT and Time report that the US and Israel plan a short, intensive operation against Iran after the midterms, and Iran promises severe retaliation. The window after the midterms runs Nov 4-15. What would make this wrong: the planned strike launches quickly in that window (about 45%). Trump has cancelled strikes before, so I set this at 0.50 rather than lower.

South Carolina is a strongly Republican state (base rate is high), but the appointee Darline Graham Nordone leads Andrews by only about 2-3 points, and Andrews has a large money advantage. One result quoted prediction-market odds; I discarded them. What would make this wrong: a weak appointee nominee plus a well-funded Democrat produces an upset (about 20-25%).

Acton leads Ramaswamy by about 3-4 points in averages (Marist +7, Fox +2, BGSU +6), and Sabato moved the race to Lean D. Ohio polls have overstated Democrats by several points in 2020-2024. What would make this wrong: that same Ohio polling bias recurs (about 40-45%). That keeps this only modestly above 50%.

Republicans hold 53-47 now. Non-market models favor Democrats: Silver Bulletin about 75%, DDHQ 56%, Poliwave 57%, VoteHub 60%; PollsMax is an outlier favoring Republicans. One aggregator showed Kalshi prices; I discarded them. What would make this wrong: a uniform polling miss toward Republicans in the Texas, Ohio, Alaska and Iowa toss-ups, as in 2016, 2020 and 2024 (about 35-40%).

Only 5 days remain. The only new agreement is a local humanitarian truce in Oleshky, which does not qualify as a general ceasefire. The next talks are set for mid-November in Abu Dhabi, and Russia rejects any pause in fighting before a comprehensive deal. What would make this wrong: a surprise Trump-brokered general truce, which is very unlikely.

Incumbent senators usually win in a state like Alaska (R+10). However, Peltola leads narrowly in most polls (averages about +1 to +2.5), and Sabato moved the race to Lean D. Ranked-choice voting has helped her before. One result quoted prediction-market odds; I discarded them. What would make this wrong: Alaska polls underestimating Republicans, as they did for Sullivan in 2020 (about 40%). That keeps this near a toss-up rather than lower.

Opus, Sonnet and Haiku 5.5 have all launched, and Fable 5.5 leaked via Azure and LiteLLM on October 13. Partner access was reported October 17, but as of October 25 there was no official announcement and only 5 days remain. What would make this wrong: Anthropic completes the 5.5 lineup this week, as the leaks suggest (about 30%). My search budget ran out before a final check.

There is an unconfirmed report of a $1B Saudi offer brokered by Iran, but Riyadh officially rejects a new ceasefire. What would make this wrong: the Tehran channel produces a quickly announced truce (about 7%).
